CaseTeamHealthOut.description:

CaughtUpOut.description: Your "since" is now: Today counts what ARGUS handled from here.

ClosurePreviewOut.description:
The exact writes asking for this closure binds: the same builder as the request's, so

ConfirmReportIn.description:
Confirm the report's verdict. Names the version read: 409 when ARGUS wrote a newer one.

CostOut.description: The AI spend for the cost bar: this month and today (UTC), against the caps.
CostOut.title: CostOut

CountsOut.description:
The Inbox's summary: investigations in each state; decided in the last 24 hours.

CountsOut.title: CountsOut

CoverageOut.description:
Alerts may be missing for this span (the collector's own outages, a rule at its alert
limit).
CoverageOut.title: CoverageOut

DashboardOut.description: The SOC dashboard (D-103) on ARGUS's own records: never a request to the SIEM.
DashboardOut.title: DashboardOut

DecisionIn.description:

DismissIn.description: Say a possible incident is not one, for a reason: the suspected case is closed.

DossierOut.description: What ARGUS checked: the newest dossier, in the words the investigation page uses.

EntityDayOut.description:

EntityPageOut.description:
What ARGUS knows of a device, account, campus site or outside address: its incidents, its
alert groups, a timeline, the notes people wrote. ``history_days``: how far back ARGUS keeps

EntityPageOut.title: EntityPageOut

ErrorOut.description: Every error: a plain sentence and a stable code.

FindingOut.description:
What the read-back saw in Kibana. ``details`` holds a person's words as they wrote them

FollowUpIn.description: Ask for a follow-up; an outcome and a note are optional.
FollowUpIn.title: FollowUpIn

Found.description: What every SIEM query of this investigation version found, against the alerts alone.

Gap.description: Something ARGUS could not tell, and who can resolve it.

GlanceItemOut.description:

GlanceLayerOut.description: One stacked series of alerts over time: a rule (or all the rest), a value per bar.

GlanceOut.description:

appear.
GlanceOut.title: GlanceOut

GoldItemOut.description: The investigation is in the gold set: the answer key's item and its newest answer.
GoldItemOut.title: GoldItemOut

GroupDecisionIn.description: Approve the rest of a group, after its sample: each request with the hash read.
GroupDecisionIn.title: GroupDecisionIn

GroupRowOut.description: An alert group (an investigation) that holds the value.

HoldIn.description:
I'm checking: what you wait on (one line, your words) and when it comes back (at most
14 days ahead).

HoldOut.description:
A person's "I'm checking" on a possible incident: it leaves everyone else's Needs you
until ``until`` (or a material change, or P1).
HoldOut.title: HoldOut

InCaseOut.description: The incident (case) an alert group belongs to: it is decided there, not on its own.
InCaseOut.title: InCaseOut

IncidentReportRowOut.description: A confirmed incident's report, newest version.
IncidentReportRowOut.title: IncidentReportRowOut

InvestigationCheckOut.description:
A person's request for one more check and its record: its state, the E-numbers its

InvestigationCheckOut.title: InvestigationCheckOut

Item.description: One line of "What ARGUS found with extra SIEM queries".
Item.title: Item

KibanaSyncOut.description: The Kibana read-back (``argus-kibana-sync``), from its newest recorded cycle.
KibanaSyncOut.title: KibanaSyncOut

KnownOut.description:
A confirmed case's owner-notified record (AR4b, D-169): who was told, the alerts ARGUS has

and the block list. ``notified_at`` is None until a person records a notice.

KnownRefOut.description:
An investigation that belongs to a notified case (AR4b, D-169): ``outcome`` is ``known``

(something is new since the notice; ``why`` says what, and it is in Needs attention).

MemberReviewsIn.description:
Mark several of one incident's alert groups at once: a verdict (an outcome) or "can't
tell yet" (``follow_up``). Each names the version and the latest review you saw. "Real: act

MergeIn.description:
Merge into another case. A confirmed case asks for an approval (``payload_hash`` from
the preview, required); a suspected case is merged at once.

MetricsOut.description:
How the assessments and the model gateway are doing (24 hours; 7 days for blocks,
floor hits and outcomes).

NewDestinationOut.description:
An address or a name a notified device reached after the notice that nobody flags and the
case did not hold. ARGUS counts it and does not raise it; if a list or the outside look-ups
flag it later, the investigation comes back as a change. The value is untrusted text.

NoteIn.description: A note alone: it does not change the investigation's state.

NoticeIn.description:
Record that the device's owner (or its department, hostel or lab) was told: who, how, and
when (default now). ARGUS then tracks the case quietly and speaks again only on change.

NoticeRecordOut.description: A notice or a block a person recorded. The words are theirs, shown as untrusted text.

NotifiedBrief.description: A case whose owner was told and that stays active (AR4b, D-169): counted, not raised.

OutboxHoldOut.description: The Kibana write an approval is about (a re-confirmation or a resend).

PatternBriefOut.description:

PatternOut.description:

PatternRecommendationOut.description:

PatternSummaryOut.description:
The patterns ARGUS recommends closing: how many there are, how many investigations they
cover, and the largest few.
PatternSummaryOut.title: PatternSummaryOut

ProposalGroupOut.description: Proposals decided the same way; confirm them together after the audit sample.

Provenance.description: Where one evidence request's answer came from: the query and what it returned.

ReminderOut.description: A suggestion from ARGUS for a notified case that stays active: never an alarm.

info.description:
The typed API of ARGUS's web app (Phase 3, Q-A1).

**Signing in** happens only on the server-rendered page `/signin` (and confirming it is you,
before an approval, on `/stepup`): no password ever passes through this API. A session is an
HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie (`__Host-argus_session` under TLS, `argus_session` on the plain
loopback). `GET /api/v1/session` says who is signed in, what they may do and when the session
ends, and gives the CSRF token: send it as `X-CSRF-Token` on every change, and keep it in
memory only.

**Every change** (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) must also come from this site's own page: an
`Origin` header equal to this server's origin (or `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`). Requests that
browsers mark as coming from another site are refused on every `/api/` path.

**Background requests** (polls, refreshes nobody asked for) send `X-Argus-Background: 1`:
they are answered as usual, but never keep a session alive. A session ends after its idle
time without a request of the person's own, and at its absolute end whatever happens.

**Errors** are always `ErrorOut {detail, code}`. On 401 send the person to
`/signin?next=<the app's path>`; on 403 `csrf` read the session again once; on 409 `conflict`
read the thing again; 429 and 503 are said plainly and never retried by the client.

**Words** (DQ23): an *investigation* is one rule, one actor and one IST day; a *case* is one
real problem across days, hosts and rules; an *incident* is a case a person confirmed.

Today: what needs a person (the queue's cases: possible incidents to confirm or
dismiss, confirmed ones nobody has taken; by band then priority; at most ten new cards a
day, P1 and P2 always), how many more of the queue wait for room, confirmed incidents
with new activity (and closed ones told of new strong evidence), the gray band (just
under a lane) and what ARGUS handled since the person's last visit, with one item to
spot-check. In shadow (``risk.present`` off) the cards are the engine's own incidents
(kind ``shadow``) and carry no case.

post.description:
Your answer to a spot-check of something ARGUS closed on its own: it looks right, it
is wrong (it should have been raised), or you cannot tell. Only what ARGUS decided
without a person is accepted (409 otherwise): an alert group it joined to an incident
that already existed or closed on its own proposal, an incident it closed itself. One
answer per person and item: answering again replaces yours. "Wrong" reopens nothing by
itself: reopen it with ``reopenCase``. The answer comes back with the team's score.
